title: Four equivalent guises of finiteness for morphisms of algebraic spaces
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a morphism of algebraic spaces over S the lemma proves the equivalence of: (1) f finite; (2) f proper and locally quasi-finite; (3) f proper with |X_k| discrete for every field-valued point of Y; (4) f universally closed, separated, locally of finite type, with the same discreteness. The retained proof is complete: (1)=>(2)=>(3)=>(4) chain through the chapter's standard permanence lemmas; the heart is (4)=>(1), written out: universal closedness gives quasi-compactness, discreteness plus qc makes each field fibre finite, the elementary etale neighbourhood splitting lemma (chapter lemma etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part) carves the fibre into a finite piece V and a remainder W whose image misses the centre, universal closedness closes the W-image so shrinking kills W entirely, etale-locally on Y the base change is finite, and integrality-is-etale-local finishes. Retained author proof at lines 7862-7900.
